title: Manchester City’s Rodri to miss Burnley game, ‘we’ll see’ over weekend return – Pep Guardiola
content:
Pep Guardiola says Manchester City midfielder Rodri will miss Wednesday’s match against Burnley due to a groin injury but could be in contention to face Southampton at the weekend.

The 29-year-old Spain international was forced off in the closing stages of City’s 2-1 win over league leaders Arsenal at the Etihad Stadium on Sunday. He went down and appeared to be in pain before being replaced by Nico Gonzalez in the 90th minute.

Guardiola said after the match that he did not know the extent of the issue and further tests would have to be done to ascertain the severity.

“I think for tomorrow he will not be ready,” the City manager told a press conference on Tuesday. “We’ll see for next games the FA Cup semi-final against Southampton or 12 days later for the Premier League game at Everton.”

Rodri has struggled with fitness issues since returning from an ACL injury sustained in September 2024, picking up a hamstring problem against Brentford on October 5 that kept him out for two months.

Since City’s draw against Brighton and Hove Albion on January 7, however, he has started every league game, both legs of their Champions League round of 16 aggregate loss to Real Madrid and the Carabao Cup final win over Arsenal.

Rodri has one year remaining on his City contract and in March said he wants to return to Spanish football one day, adding he “could not turn down” the opportunity of playing for Real Madrid.

Sunday’s win moved City to within three points of Arsenal, with one game in hand, and they can take top spot with victory against Burnley.

“Arsenal is top of the league, if it finishes right now they will be champions,” Guardiola added. “We have to see how they (the players) recover not just the demanding game that we had emotionally and physically.

“Six games left, we know exactly what might happen with or without results.”
